english.title: Criminal damage to property - value over £5000
english.standardoffencewording:
On **(..SPECIFY DATE..) at **(..SPECIFY TOWNSHIP..) without lawful excuse,

(A)_[destroyed **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..)]_
(B)_[damaged **(..SPECIFY PROPERTY..)]_

to the value of **(..SPECIFY VALUE OVER FIVE THOUSAND POUNDS..) belonging to **(..SPECIFY NAME..) intending to destroy or damage such property or being reckless as to whether such property would be destroyed or damaged
english.legislation: Contrary to sections 1(1) and 4 of the Criminal Damage Act 1971.

english.notes:
(i) See offence wording: H2082 - where the damage involved is less than five thousand pounds in value.
(ii) Property damaged/destroyed must not belong to defendant(s).
(iii) Consent of the Director of Public Prosecutions is required where damage is to spouse's property (section 30(4) of the Theft Act 1968).
(iv) See guidelines on mode of trial.
(v) The same incident may involve separate activities, some causing ordinary damage and some damage by fire (for example, protestors break into a laboratory building, smash laboratory equipment and set fire to some files). In such circumstances they are separate offences and best charged as such (R v Booth and others1999).

other.penalty:
Either way:
SUMMARY: Six months imprisonment and / or a fine not exceeding the statutory maximum.
INDICTMENT: Ten years imprisonment.

Time limit for prosecutions:
None
